label: The design effect for an exchangeable within-subject correlation is one plus (T minus one) times rho, where T is the number of visits and rho the intra-class correlation
The paired t statistic is the mean of the per-subject differences, d-bar, divided by the standard error of that mean, which is the standard deviation of the differences over the square root of n
The standard error of the mean paired difference is the square root of two sigma squared times (one minus rho) divided by n, where rho is the within-subject correlation
The Wilcoxon signed-rank test statistic W is the smaller of W-plus, the sum of the ranks of the positive differences, and W-minus, the sum of the ranks of the negative differences
The repeated-measures ANOVA F statistic is the mean square for time divided by the mean square for the time by subject interaction, which serves as the error term

The mixed-effects model with a random intercept: the observation y for subject s at visit t equals beta zero plus beta one times t, plus the subject random effect b subscript s, plus the residual e for s at t
